correctness.rationale: In normal coordinates the Hessian of half the squared distance has radial and transverse eigenvalues 1 and q=rS'_K/S_K. Expanding the coordinate quotients gives G=g+Bu+O(‖u‖²) with B=H/2 plus the skew term (H_12/2)J, J taking E_1 to E_2. The local implicit displacement is −hg+h²Bg+O(h³). Since g=−r e_r is an eigenvector of H and H_12=(q−1)sinθ cosθ, the inward-to-azimuthal skew term is exactly r(1−q)sin(2θ)/4. A radial exponential displacement changes no azimuth, so the leading angular increment is the transverse displacement divided by S_K, with error O(h³). The recurrence r_{j+1}=r_j−hr_j+O(h²) on a compact annulus slightly larger than [r_0 exp(−T),r_0], still in the smooth region, gives a uniform O(h) deviation by bootstrap and discrete Gronwall. Summing angular increments and dividing by h gives the integral in (10); (r/S_K)'=(1−q)/S_K and r'=-r give exactly (1). The opposite strict monotonicities of r/S_K in the two curved cases, and its constant value in the flat case, give the exact signs and maximizing angles. Reversing the coordinate order negates the skew term, proving O(h²) fixed-time angular error for the average. At θ=π/4 the intermediate exponential images for a radial candidate are radial-meridian reflections, with equal objective values, and the two components telescope to the radial secant −r+δ/2. Solving δ=h(r−δ/2) gives (2), with 0<δ<r for 0<h<2 and agreement with the locally unique small-h branch.
residual_risks: The informal sign phrase 'positively oriented frame' should be read as sin(2θ)>0, such as θ=π/4, as determined by (1); determinant orientation alone does not fix the sign. When sin(2θ)<0 both curved signs reverse.

The exact all-0<h<2 statement is existence of the radial bisector branch; there is no assertion of uniqueness among all large-step roots. Fixed-time convergence uses the stipulated angle at every iterate and a smooth polar chart away from the center and cut locus.
The frozen script uses bounded mesh refinements and finite tolerances, not a uniform proof or an independent numerical run.

value.rationale: Even on a canonical objective whose exact trajectory has no angular motion, the ordered dissipative scheme can accumulate a signed first-order azimuth bias, reversed by curvature and by frame order. Its sharp coefficient measures an error invisible in radial dissipation or a generic convergence order. The exact bisector identity is a useful separate benchmark for the established symmetric variant.
